outcome: The Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture (the modern operator-theoretic form of the volume conjecture) was proved for a new large class of one-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds admitting 'FAMED' geometric triangulations, including all knots in S3 with at most 12 crossings and all knots with a triangulation of 23 or fewer tetrahedra (over 42,000 knots verified); additional papers proved the (Chen-Yang variant of the) conjecture for large-parameter Dehn fillings of twist-knot manifolds and, separately, for all hyperbolic double twist knots. The general conjecture, for arbitrary hyperbolic knots, remains open.
summary: Since 26 January 2024 there has been real, substantive progress on cases of the volume conjecture, but no AI or machine-learning system was involved in producing any of it, and the general conjecture (for arbitrary hyperbolic knots) is still open. The most significant development is the 'FAMED geometric triangulations' program: Ohtsuki and collaborators introduced FAMED triangulations in an October 2024 preprint (arXiv:2410.10776, submitted 2024-10-14) and proved that the Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture (the version of the conjecture phrased via Teichmuller TQFT partition functions and the Neumann-Zagier potential, closely related to Kashaev's original invariant) holds for every hyperbolic 3-manifold admitting such a triangulation, exhibiting these for every hyperbolic twist knot and the first 42,000 hyperbolic knots in S3. A December 2025 follow-up (arXiv:2512.17437, 'Famed by computer') extends this by computational search (using Regina and SnapPy) to all knots with at most 12 crossings and all knots whose complement triangulates with at most 23 tetrahedra, again over 42,000 examples. This is scope-appropriate: it settles the stated conjecture for a large but restricted class of knot complements (a case, not the whole problem), so it is classified 'partial' with direction 'confirmed' (the conjecture held for every example checked; no counterexample was found or claimed). The role of the computer here (Regina/SnapPy triangulation enumeration) is exhaustive rigorous search/computer algebra, not an AI system, so ai_role is 'none'. Two further preprints add other partial results within the window: arXiv:2501.00225 (submitted 2024-12-31, revised through May 2025) proves the volume conjecture for all hyperbolic double twist knots using complexified tetrahedra and SL(2,C) representations, with no AI or ML mentioned anywhere in the methodology; arXiv:2410.20489 (submitted 2024-10-27) proves the Chen-Yang variant of the volume conjecture (a related but distinct q-deformation with q approaching a root of unity along the unit circle rather than 1) for Dehn-filled twist-knot manifolds, but only for sufficiently large Dehn-filling parameters, which is itself a further restriction. A February 2025 preprint (arXiv:2502.18575) trains a feedforward neural network to predict hyperbolic volume from the adjoint Jones polynomial (99.34% accuracy) and uses this purely as a numerical exploration tool to motivate an improved conjectural statement about the optimal phase for colored Jones polynomial asymptotics; the network's output is not itself a proof, is not incorporated into any theorem, and the authors show a closed-form function of the polynomial achieves comparable accuracy without any learning, so this is 'none' involvement (a numerics-motivated conjecture refinement, not a case of the stated problem being settled, and not AI-produced mathematics). No expert digestion (Tao's blog, Quanta, a survey) of the FAMED result was found, and it has not appeared in a journal; the December 2025 preprint is very recent (this deep dive is dated 2026-09-22, about 9 months after that preprint), so it is plausible a digestion exists that a search did not surface, but none was found. Given the absence of expert digestion or journal acceptance, and that these are all preprints, the correct status is 'partial' (a case was settled) rather than 'resolved' — no single event fully resolves the general conjecture, and the individual case-results themselves are still only preprints. The event date recorded is the first (Oct 2024) FAMED preprint, the earliest genuinely new post-window result found; the December 2025 computational extension and the double-twist-knot and Chen-Yang results are described here rather than given separate records, per the instruction to consolidate on one decisive event and describe others in summary.
competing_reading: One could argue the December 2025 'Famed by computer' preprint (2512.17437), rather than the October 2024 theory preprint (2410.10776), should be the dated 'event', since it is the one that actually reaches the widely-quoted '42,000+ knots, all ≤12 crossings' headline figure via computer search; the October 2024 paper proves the general FAMED criterion and applies it to twist knots and an initial batch of 42,000 knots, so the two papers' claimed knot counts overlap and the later paper is best read as extending the computational search rather than being the first appearance of the result. Either dating supports the same 'partial' classification. Separately, one could argue the Chen-Yang large-parameter Dehn-filling result and the neural-network-motivated conjecture refinement are 'related problems' (different q-limits, or a different conjectural statement) rather than cases of the stated conjecture, in which case they would not count toward this record at all; I have read them as adjacent partial evidence worth mentioning rather than as the load-bearing event, so this reading does not change the recorded status.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (a survey, a blog post by a specialist such as Ohtsuki or a Quanta/Tao-style write-up) confirming the FAMED-triangulation proof is correct and assessing how much of the knot volume conjecture landscape it now covers would move the FAMED result from 'partial-preprint' toward a stronger evidentiary footing; journal acceptance of any of these preprints would strengthen confidence further. A search of the Kashaev invariant / volume conjecture literature for any AI-lab announcement (e.g. a foundation-model mathematics team claiming a proof) between January 2024 and September 2026 turned up nothing, so nothing here is contingent on missing an AI claim, only on missing an expert readthrough of preprints that already exist.
